newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares ease, seen inching up on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares ease, seen inching up on Monday.

text.p: Polish shares eased on Friday, falling for the fourth session running in profit-taking, but analysts said the market should rise slightly on Monday, signalled by Friday's strong buying after price-fixing.

"Monday and Tuesday will test demand. Yesterday and today tested supply, which is falling, and now the question is if there'll be demand on Monday and Tuesday...If not, growth could end after one or two sessions," said Pawel Tarnowski, an analyst at Raiffeisen Capital and Investment.
Some analysts said primary market offers next month could prevent the recent stock-buying frenzy from returning.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.4 percent to 16,105.5 points and turnover fell 15.5 percent to 134.3 million zlotys ($44.8 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 50 to 21 with 15 stocks flat.

Analysts said biggest loser Bank Gdanski, which fell 6.1 percent, may have been hurt by a feud between the supervisory board and managing firm of the mass privatisation National Investment Fund (NFI) to which Gdanski belongs.
Analysts were surprised by the scale of top gainer builder Exbud's 6.9 percent rise in moderate trade.
